laterChanges: For 2025 assessments/pay2026, SEA 1 adds a supplemental homestead credit of the lesser of $300 or 10% of liability, a $150 over-65 credit, and a $125 blind/disabled credit; it changes senior eligibility and deductions.
name: Indiana
overview: Indiana's statutory circuit-breaker labels include assessed-value tax caps and a separate income-limited senior tax-growth credit.

programs.name: Property Tax Cap / Circuit Breaker Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Credit offsets covered homestead taxes exceeding 1% of gross assessed value.
programs.formulaSummary: Caps covered homestead tax at 1% of gross assessed value; other residential property generally has a 2% cap.
eligibilityNotes: Certain voter-approved levies can remain outside the caps.
programs.programYear: 2025 payable property-tax bills; value-based rather than income-based cap.

sources.title: Indiana property-tax circuit-breaker caps fact sheet

programs.name: Over 65 Circuit Breaker Credit
programs.ageRule: Qualifying senior homeowner age 65+; surviving-spouse rules apply.
programs.incomeDefinition: Federal adjusted gross income from the calendar year two years before taxes are payable.
programs.incomeLimits: Indexed limits depend on pay year; use the DLGF historical table for pay 2025.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualifying reduction needed to limit annual homestead tax growth to 2%.
programs.formulaSummary: Uses prior-year liability, age/income tests, and the applicable assessment-year eligibility rules.
programs.application: Apply through county auditor using senior property-tax benefits form.
eligibilityNotes: 2024 assessment/pay2025 has a $240,000 assessed-value eligibility limit.
programs.programYear: Pay 2025 baseline; assessment 2024, generally uses 2023 AGI.

sources.title: Over-65 credit income thresholds, pay-year table

programs.name: Renter's income-tax deduction
programs.maximumBenefit: Deduction of up to $3,000, or $1,500 married filing separately; this is not the tax saving.
programs.formulaSummary: Lesser of qualifying rent or the filing-status deduction cap reduces taxable income.
eligibilityNotes: Principal Indiana residence subject to property tax required.

programs.name: Homeowner residential property-tax deduction
programs.maximumBenefit: Deduction up to $2,500, or $1,250 married filing separately.
programs.formulaSummary: Lesser of principal-residence property taxes paid or deduction cap reduces taxable income.
programs.application: Claim on the Indiana income-tax return.

researchNotes: A value-based cap is not an income-threshold circuit breaker despite the shared statutory name.
New model variables beginning 2026 must not be applied to pay2025 bills.
Assessment year versus payable year must remain visible in comparisons.
